therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: protein degradation pathway disruption in myeloma cells
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: participants with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma not treated with stem cell transplantation

results.effect_size: median PFS 17.4 months vs 9.4 months (HR not provided for primary endpoint)
results.target_engagement_evidence: plasma concentrations measured showing drug exposure with geometric mean concentrations ranging from 1.683-19.353 ng/mL across cycles
biomarker_changes: 6% of ixazomib patients converted from MRD positive to MRD negative vs 3% placebo
MRD negative patients had longer PFS than MRD positive patients
subgroup_findings: No benefit in high-risk cytogenetics population (HR 1.011, p=0.963)
Benefit maintained across frailty status subgroups with strongest effect in fit patients (HR 0.530, p<0.001)
safety_signals: Higher rate of treatment-emergent adverse events (92% vs 82%)
Higher rate of serious adverse events (24% vs 17%)
Peripheral neuropathy with longer time to resolution (451 vs 196 days)
results.dose_information: oral ixazomib capsules, specific dose not provided in results
